items.caption: An oracle-script style form of 喜 places a branched upper shape above a rounded lower enclosure. The upper shape is analyzed as 壴, an upright drum graph, and the lower as 口; the proposed drum-and-singing motivation is an interpretation, not a meaning visible in the strokes.
items.alt: Black oracle-script style character with a tall branched upper part and a rounded lower enclosure containing a short horizontal stroke.
items.selection_reason: This redraw gives a useful visual example of an oracle-script style form alongside the reported 壴-and-口 analysis. The component interpretation and its proposed association with joy remain scholarly explanations.

items.caption: A small-seal style form of 喜 has a branched upper shape above two enclosed sections. Shuowen analyzes 喜 as formed from 壴 and 口, but that lexicographic account does not independently confirm the proposed drum-and-singing motivation.
items.alt: Black small-seal style character with a branched top, a rounded middle enclosure, and a broad lower enclosure.
items.selection_reason: This distinct script-style example complements the oracle-style form and illustrates a later recorded category. The redraw does not establish a dated sequence of graphic changes.

limitations.text: The drum-and-singing account is a proposed explanation of the graph’s motivation. Other interpretations have been offered, and oracle-bone examples are reported with both joy and name uses without secure dates establishing their order.
These illustrations are modern redrawings of script styles, not photographs of inscribed objects. Their script labels do not establish a dated sequence of forms.
